History of Present Illness:
28-year-old man. Pain started diffusely twelve hours ago and is now concentrated in the right lower abdomen. He has nausea but no vomiting.

Physical Examination:
Focal right lower-quadrant tenderness; abdomen soft away from this area. Temperature 38.0 C; heart rate 94/min; BP 128/70 mmHg; respiratory rate 18/min; SpO2 97% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 12.9 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.1 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 262 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 136 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.7 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 99 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 38 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 28 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 31 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 97 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: noncompressible blind-ending tubular structure arising from the cecum, 9 mm in diameter, with mural hyperemia and echogenic surrounding fat.
